To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the addition of a nanoparticle component to chemical vapor deposition of SiC results in an improvement of the hardness, indentation modulus, and fracture toughness of the resulting coatings, and that the relative contributions of chemical vapor deposition and particle impaction are determined by the substrate temperature and can be used to tailor the resulting film properties.
we were able to deposit a nanostructured SiC film with a hardness of 39 GPa and a fracture toughness of 6 MPa·m1/2.

the synthesis method combines chemical vapor deposition (to provide a high density film with a low porosity) and nanoparticle impactions (to provide a film with a high hardness and high fracture toughness).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of nanostructured SiC films using a combination of chemical vapor deposition with nanoparticle impactions.

the development of novel, low-cost synthesis techniques that produce SiC films with high mechanical strength and fracture toughness, while maintaining the high temperature capabilities of the material.
the development of a new process for producing nanostructured SiC coatings that combine the advantages of chemical vapor deposition and nanoparticles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the nanoparticle impaction process is a viable method to deposit nanostructured SiC coatings, and that the CVD process can enhance film properties by reducing porosity and enhancing chemical vapor deposition.
the combination of CVD and nanoparticle impactions is a viable method for the synthesis of nanostructured SiC coatings.
the combination of CVD and nanoparticle impactions results in nanostructured films that exhibit improved hardness and toughness over conventional CVD films.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of CVD with nanoparticles is an effective means for producing nanostructured films.
the nanoparticle synthesis process can be used to produce nanostructured SiC films that are superior to those grown by CVD alone.
nanoparticle impaction can be combined with chemical vapor deposition to create nanostructured coatings with improved mechanical properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the nanoparticle contribution to the film growth does not have to be eliminated in order to produce a dense coating with good mechanical properties.
the combination of CVD and nanoparticle impactions is an effective means to produce SiC coatings with a combination of desirable mechanical properties.
the nanoparticle impaction technique provides a new method of producing high hardness, high fracture toughness SiC nanostructured films that can compete with the best commercial films.
